AI begins long before the data centre.

Explore the physical chain.
See what is counted—and what is still missing.

→→→
There is no defensible single total for the entire AI supply chain in these sources.

The 155 TWh estimate covers operating AI-focused data centres. Adding all of TSMC, telecom networks or supplier emissions would count non-AI activity and mix incompatible measures. Carbon emissions cannot be converted to electricity without a source-specific model.

07 / UNDER THE NUMBERS

Transparent by design.

Download data ↓Open source ↗

A watt is a rate.

GW measures power at an instant. TWh measures electricity over time. A constant 1 GW for 365 days is 8.76 TWh. The “Average GW” view uses the hours in the reported year; 2024 has 366 days.

Boundaries matter.

World and country demand includes system losses. City and company figures usually measure consumption closer to the meter. Ratios are scale analogies, not exact shares of a harmonised accounting total.

Estimates stay estimates.

Country and company data describe reported periods. AI data is modelled. Dashed lines are projections or labelled illustrations. Renewable matching does not reduce the number of TWh used.

Curated snapshot researched 14 September 2026. Source years vary; this is not a live power meter. Reported figures may be revised. All comparisons describe electricity, not all forms of energy or climate impact.
